summary: This bill excludes from gross income any capital gain on the sale of U.S. farm real property (used for farming at least 2 of the prior 8 years) when sold to a spouse, lineal descendant, or their spouse, with carryover basis and a 10-year holding period for later basis adjustment.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a tax exclusion for capital gains on intra-family farm transfers. It affects federal revenue but does not authorize, expand, or reduce any direct government spending programs or appropriations. Therefore it has no bearing on government spending.

The core provision adds new IRC section 121A that excludes from gross income any gain realized on the sale or exchange of qualified farm property to a qualified family member. This is a direct, targeted reduction in capital-gains taxation for a defined class of transactions. The bill therefore clearly moves in the direction of lower taxes.
The bill contains no provisions related to health insurance, medical providers, public health programs, or market-based healthcare reforms.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address visas, border security, asylum, or any immigration pathways.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions affect defense authorizations, military construction, or defense spending levels.
No provisions alter environmental regulations, land-use restrictions, or climate policy.
No provisions modify eligibility, funding, or administration of welfare, SNAP, Medicaid, or similar programs.
No provisions address schools, school choice, federal education funding, or student aid.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal procedure.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.

The revenue loss from the new exclusion would increase the deficit in the absence of offsetting measures, but the bill itself contains no language about debt reduction, deficit targets, or fiscal offsets. The connection is too indirect to register a nonzero score.
No provisions address legal protections, benefits, or nondiscrimination rules for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance, international development, or State Department funding.
No provisions address voter access, election administration, or campaign finance.
No provisions address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance.
No provisions address collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rules.
No provisions address religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and antidiscrimination rules.

The bill creates a new exclusion from gross income for capital gains on transfers of qualified farm property to family members, directly reducing federal tax revenue with no offsetting revenue raisers or spending cuts. Because the entire legislation is devoted to this tax relief, the measure would increase the deficit.
